To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed lazy safety controller design for incrementaly stable switched systems with event-based symbolic models is more efficient than the one designed with classical symbolic models.

we propose a novel event-based design scheme for symbolic models of switched systems with a periodical time sampling and that we show that the resulting symbolic models are useful for the synthesis of lazy safety controllers.

we provide a novel method to design lazy safety controllers for incrementally stable discrete-time switched systems with a period time sampling, based on event-based symbolic models, and that the obtained lazy safety controllers have a better performance than the classical safety controllers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of lazy safety controllers for switched systems.
the design of lazy safety controllers for event-based symbolic representations of switched systems.
the problem of lazy controllers design for switched systems with a periodical time sampling and aperiodic triggering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the obtained symbolic models are useful for lazy control design of incrementally stable systems and that the proposed event-based symbolic models are related to classical symbolic models designed with periodic time sampling by a feedback refinement.

, in comparison to the classical symbolic models, the obtained event-based ones are more suitable for control applications since they provide larger sets of controllable states and thus better control performances.
the event-based scheme is more efficient than the periodic one for the lazy safety controller design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the obtained eventbased symbolic model of an incrementally stable switched system can be used for control applications.
the obtained results are of practical interest for control applications and that our approach is suitable for control design of large-scale complex switched systems.
the event-based symbolic models are more suitable for the synthesis of lazy safety controllers than the classical symbolic models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the event-based symbolic models provide a better trade-off between precision and computational resources when compared with the classical ones.

the obtained eventbased symbolic models can be used for control purposes and that the lazy controller designed for these models can lead to a better performance than the one designed for the classical models.
the obtained lazy safety controllers are more efficient than the classical safety controllers in terms of the size of the controllable set of states.
